Forecast Discussion

A front stalled to our southeast has delivered a quick shot of drier air to the region, limiting afternoon & evening showers & storms to only isolated levels for Saturday. Coverage looks perhaps slightly greater on Sunday as the front drifts back towards us a smidge, but still limited.

The main story for next week will be the presence of a strengthening upper-level ridge sliding over the area from the west. We have spent much of August (especially the first half) with a ridge positioned to our west, leaving us in a more active northwest flow and producing a rather wet month for many. That story changes to end August & start September, as the ridge looks to dominate our weather into late next week.

Isolated showers & storms remain the expectation in the mountains each day, but the majority will be dry… and plenty warm. Enjoy Saturday, as it is the coolest day of the forecast. Tuesday through Thursday of next week bring the peak of the heat, with near-record values possible each day as the ridge sits overhead.

Some measure of relief appears possible for the start of Labor Day weekend, as a weakening in the ridge allows for a trough to drop down from the north and potentially bring a backdoor cool front with it. This may serve to produce a few more afternoon showers, and would certainly beat back the heat.
